# Downloads and Web APIs {#chp:web}

Fetching a file, checking that a link is alive, asking GitHub for the latest
release: these chores all hit the network. The examples that need a connection
are shown but not run here; the URL-parsing helpers work offline and are run.

## Work with URLs {#sec:grp-web-url}

Parse a URL and check where it leads.

### Pull the file name out of a URL {#sec:url-filename}

Query strings and hashes make `basename()` unreliable on URLs. `url_filename()`
strips them, and falls back to a default when the URL ends in a slash or a bare
domain. It is pure string work, so no request is sent:

```{r}
url_filename(c(
  'https://yihui.org/images/logo.png',
  'https://yihui.org/index.html?foo=bar#about',
  'https://yihui.org/'
))
url_filename('https://yihui.org', default = 'home.html')
```

### Check that a link is alive {#sec:url-accessible}

`url_accessible()` sends a `HEAD` request and returns `TRUE` if the status is
below 400, `FALSE` otherwise (including when the request fails outright):

```r
url_accessible('https://yihui.org')
url_accessible('https://yihui.org/no-such-page-here')
```

Handy for filtering a vector of links: `Filter(url_accessible, urls)`.

### Find where a redirect really goes {#sec:url-destination}

Short links and canonical URLs redirect. `url_destination()` follows the
`Location` header and returns the final address, or the original URL if there is
no redirect. Status codes of 400 and above raise an error. Results are cached
for the session; use `force = TRUE` to ask again:

```r
url_destination('https://cran.r-project.org/package=xfun')
url_destination('https://cran.r-project.org/package=xfun', force = TRUE)
```

## Download files {#sec:grp-web-download}

Fetch a file, and fetch it only once.

### Download a file, whatever works {#sec:download-file}

`download.file()` has several methods, and which one works depends on the
machine and proxy. `download_file()` tries them all (libcurl, curl, wget,
wininet, ...) and stops with an error only if none succeeds. The output
defaults to the file name from `url_filename()`:

```r
f = download_file('https://yihui.org/images/logo.png')
f  # "logo.png", the path of the downloaded file

download_file('https://yihui.org/images/logo.png', tempfile(fileext = '.png'))
```

It returns the output path. Extra arguments go to `download.file()`. The
`timeout` option is raised to an hour for the call if you left it at the default
60 seconds, so big files are fine.

### Download once, reuse forever {#sec:download-cache}

`download_cache` is an object of methods that saves downloads on disk, so a
second request for the same URL is instant (and works offline):

```r
x1 = download_cache$get('https://www.r-project.org/')  # downloads
x2 = download_cache$get('https://www.r-project.org/')  # from cache
identical(x1, x2)

# binary file, or transform the content once and cache the result
logo = download_cache$get('https://yihui.org/images/logo.png', 'raw')
n = download_cache$get('https://www.r-project.org/', 'text', nchar)
```

The `type` is `'text'`, `'raw'`, `'base64'`, or the default `'auto'`, which
picks text or raw from the response headers. Manage the cache with the other
methods:

```r
download_cache$summary()  # what is cached, with sizes
download_cache$remove('https://yihui.org/images/logo.png', 'raw')
download_cache$purge()    # delete everything
```

## REST APIs {#sec:grp-web-rest}

Read JSON or the raw response from a web API.

### Read JSON from a REST API {#sec:rest-api}

`rest_api()` sends a `GET` request and parses the JSON reply into a list.
Give it a root, an endpoint, and optionally a token and query parameters:

```r
res = rest_api('https://mockhttp.org', '/get')
str(res)

# query parameters, and an authorization token
rest_api('https://mockhttp.org', '/response-headers',
  params = list(foo = 'bar'))
rest_api('https://mockhttp.org', '/headers', token = 'YOUR_TOKEN')
```

By default the token is sent as `Authorization: Basic TOKEN`; name it to change
the scheme, e.g. `token = c(Bearer = 'YOUR_TOKEN')`. Only `GET` is supported.
For `POST` and friends, use the curl or httr package. `rest_api()` needs
jsonlite.

### Get the raw response instead {#sec:rest-api-raw}

If the API returns something other than JSON, or you prefer your own parser,
`rest_api_raw()` takes the same arguments and returns the response text
untouched. Extra request headers go in `headers`:

```r
txt = rest_api_raw('https://mockhttp.org', '/get',
  headers = c(Accept = 'application/json'))
cat(txt)
```

## GitHub {#sec:grp-web-github}

Ask GitHub for repository data.

### Call the GitHub API {#sec:github-api}

`github_api()` is `rest_api_raw()` pointed at `https://api.github.com`, with
token handling built in. It reads a token from the `token` argument or from the
`GITHUB_PAT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `GH_TOKEN` environment variables. Without one
you get only 60 calls an hour:

```r
repo = github_api('/repos/yihui/xfun')
repo$stargazers_count

github_api('/repos/yihui/xfun/issues', params = list(state = 'open'))
github_api('/repos/yihui/xfun', raw = TRUE)  # unparsed JSON text
```

The reply is parsed when jsonlite is available, raw text otherwise. Set the
token in the environment rather than in code:
`Sys.setenv(GITHUB_PAT = 'YOUR_TOKEN')`, ideally in `~/.Renviron`.

### List a repository's release tags {#sec:github-releases}

`github_releases()` returns release tags, filtered by a regular expression
(default `'v[0-9.]+'`). Pass a tag to check that it exists, or `'latest'` for
the newest release:

```r
github_releases('yihui/litedown')
github_releases('gohugoio/hugo', 'latest')
github_releases('yihui/xfun', pattern = 'v0[.]4[0-9.]*')
```

## Upload files {#sec:grp-web-upload}

Send a file to an FTP server or an image host.

### Upload a file to an FTP server {#sec:upload-ftp}

`upload_ftp()` runs `curl -T file server` when the curl command exists, and
falls back to the curl package otherwise. It returns the status code, where `0`
means success for the command-line route:

```r
upload_ftp('report.pdf', 'ftp://user:PASSWORD@ftp.example.com', dir = 'reports')
```

### Host an image on Imgur {#sec:upload-imgur}

`upload_imgur()` uploads an image and returns its public link, which is useful
for documents that should point to hosted images instead of local files. With
`include_xml = TRUE`, the full response from Imgur is attached as an attribute:

```r
f = tempfile(fileext = '.png')
png(f); plot(1:10); dev.off()

link = upload_imgur(f, key = 'YOUR_IMGUR_CLIENT_ID')
link
attr(link, 'XML')  # only with include_xml = TRUE

# or set the key once
options(xfun.upload_imgur.key = 'YOUR_IMGUR_CLIENT_ID')
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`upload_ftp()` and `upload_imgur()` send your files to third-party servers.
Imgur uploads are public to anyone with the link. Without your own client ID,
`upload_imgur()` uses a shared one registered by the xfun author, which can hit
rate limits, so register your own.
:::
